narr: A small complex of showers and thunderstorms spread southeast into the northern sections of Southwest Arkansas during the morning hours of May 12th with the passage of an upper level disturbance. While these showers and thunderstorms remained non-severe as they moved into Southwest Arkansas, a very moist air mass coupled with the slow movement of these storms allowed for the development of locally heavy rainfall which produced amounts of one to in excess of three inches in a short period of time across Southern Howard, Northern Hempstead, and Northern Nevada Counties before diminishing by late morning. This resulted in instances of flooding across these areas throughout the morning hours.
